/-!
# Erdős Problem 357

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/357](https://www.erdosproblems.com/357)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos357

open Filter Asymptotics

def HasDistinctSums {ι α : Type*} [Preorder ι] [AddCommMonoid α] (a : ι → α) : Prop :=
  {J : Finset ι | (J : Set ι).OrdConnected}.InjOn (fun J ↦ ∑ x ∈ J, a x)

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. -/
noncomputable def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | ∃ a : Fin k → ℤ, Set.range a ⊆ Set.Icc 1 n ∧ StrictMono a ∧ HasDistinctSums a}

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. Is $f(n)=o(n)$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.i : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/-
Formalisation note: the next 5 formalisations are an attempt at capturing the question "how does
$f(n)$ grow?". In addition to trivial solutions (e.g. setting `answer(sorry) = 0` in some of these),
it is possible that some of these admit easy solutions that shouldn't count as genuine solutions.
As usual in this repo, solving this problem is not simply providing a term to replace `answer(sorry)`
together with a proof of the theorem, but providing a *mathematically interesting* answer.
Note also that there might be other reasonable (and non equivalent) formal statements that capture this
question.
Similar remarks hold for the `variants.monotone` formalisations later in this file.
-/

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
How does $f(n)$ grow? Can we find a (good) explicit function $g$ such that $g = O(f)$ ? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.bigO_version :
    (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =O[atTop] (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
How does $f(n)$ grow? Can we find a (good) explicit function $g$ such that $f = O(g)$ ? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.bigO_version_symm :
    (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
How does $f(n)$ grow? Can we find a (good) explicit function $g$ such that $f = \Theta(g)$ ? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.bigTheta_version :
    (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =Θ[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
How does $f(n)$ grow? Can we find a (good) explicit function $g$ such that $g = o(f)$ ? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version :
    (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
How does $f(n)$ grow? Can we find a (good) explicit function $g$ such that $f = o(g)$ ? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version_symm :
    (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct.
It is known that $f(n) \geq (2+o(1))\sqrt{n}$.
Source: See comment by Desmond Weisenberg here: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/357.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.variants.weisenberg : ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (2 + o n) * √n ≤ f n := by
  sorry

/-- Suppose $A$ is an infinite set such that all finite sums of consecutive terms of $A$ are distinct.
Then $A$ has lower density 0. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_lower_density (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : StrictMono A)
    (hA : HasDistinctSums A) : (Set.range A).lowerDensity = 0 := by
  sorry

/--  Suppose $A$ is an infinite set such that all finite sums of consecutive terms of $A$ are distinct.
Then it is conjectured that $A$ has density 0. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_density (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : StrictMono A)
    (hA : HasDistinctSums A) :
    (Set.range A).HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry


/-- Suppose $A$ is an infinite set such that all finite sums of consecutive terms of $A$ are distinct.
Then it is conjectured that the sum $\sum_k \frac{1}{a_k}$ converges. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.variants.infinite_set_sum (A : ℕ → ℕ) (hA : StrictMono A)
    (hA : HasDistinctSums A) :
    Summable (fun i ↦ (1 : ℝ) / A i) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $g(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1, \dotsc, a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. -/
noncomputable def g (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | ∃ a : Fin k → ℕ, (Set.range a ⊆ Set.Icc 1 n) ∧ HasDistinctSums a}

/-- Let $g(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1, \dotsc, a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. It is known that
$$\left(\frac 1 3 + o(1) \right)n \leq g(n) \leq \left(\frac 2 3 + o(1) \right)n.$$ -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.variants.hegyvari : ∃ (o o' : ℕ → ℝ), o =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    o' =o[atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
      ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (g n : ℝ) ∈ Set.Icc ((1 / 3 + o n) * n) ((2 / 3 + o' n)*n) := by
  sorry

/-- Let $h(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 \leq \dotsc \leq a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. -/
noncomputable def h (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | ∃ a : Fin k → ℤ, Set.range a ⊆ Set.Icc 1 n ∧ Monotone a ∧ HasDistinctSums a}

findings.description:
`h n` is the sSup over `k` such that some `a : Fin k → ℤ` satisfies `Monotone a ∧ HasDistinctSums a`. The problem is that `HasDistinctSums a` also compares the one-term intervals `{i}` and `{j}` (both are order-connected), so it already forces `a i ≠ a j` for `i ≠ j`. On the linear order `Fin k`, monotone plus injective is `StrictMono`. So `h = f` for every n. I proved `theorem h_eq_f : h = f` in a scratch file importing the module (using `Monotone.strictMono_of_injective`; code in notes).

The consequence is that the variant the source describes, which explicitly allows repeated terms, is not formalized: no sequence admissible for `h` can have a_i = a_j. The six theorems `Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.monotone.parts.i`, `...monotone.parts.ii.bigO_version`, `...bigO_version_symm`, `...bigTheta_version`, `...littleO_version` and `...littleO_version_symm` are exactly `erdos_357.parts.i` and the five `erdos_357.parts.ii.*` statements. Each `↔` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, which I checked in Lean. The file's comment, "it's not clear whether the difficulty is the same as for the strictly monotone case", is also wrong: it is the same problem.

Concrete comparison by brute force for n = 1..8:
- the file's h(n) = f(n) = 1,2,2,3,4,4,5,5;
- the reading suggested on the source's forum (never compare two one-term sums) gives 2,3,4,4,5,6,7,7.
For example, (1,1) should be admissible for n = 1 once a_i = a_j is allowed. A variant that really allows repeated terms is therefore a different function.
findings.source_evidence:
erdosproblems.com/357 (last edited 12 Jan 2026; read via web.archive.org snapshot 20260824195413) says: "A similar question can be asked if we replace strict monotonicity with weak monotonicity (i.e. we allow $a_i=a_j$)."

The forum thread erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/357 discusses exactly this point:
- Moritz Firsching, 3 Feb 2026: "I'm not quite sure how to make sense of this: Is the idea here to then allow only sums over intervals of length larger than 1? or is it then allowed to take sums over length-1 intervals, but they are only counted once? ... Boris Alexeev pointed me to this question when asking about our formalisation in Formal Conjectures of this problem."
- Adenwalla: the original [ErGr80, p.58] only says "What if we remove the monotonicity constraint and/or the distinctness constraint?"
- Adenwalla again: "I think a good interpretation of weak monotonicity is one where we don't compare sums over two different length 1 intervals ... and the rest is the same."
findings.suggested_fix:
Two options:
1. Delete `h` and the six `variants.monotone.*` theorems, since they duplicate `parts.*`.
2. Give the variant a distinctness condition that lets terms repeat, state the chosen reading in the docstring, and remove the comment about uncertain relative difficulty. For example, a condition under which two one-term sums are never compared:
`def HasDistinctSumsWeak {ι α : Type*} [Preorder ι] [AddCommMonoid α] (a : ι → α) : Prop := ∀ J₁ J₂ : Finset ι, (J₁ : Set ι).OrdConnected → (J₂ : Set ι).OrdConnected → J₁ ≠ J₂ → (2 ≤ J₁.card ∨ 2 ≤ J₂.card) → ∑ x ∈ J₁, a x ≠ ∑ x ∈ J₂, a x`
and then
`h n := sSup {k | ∃ a : Fin k → ℤ, Set.range a ⊆ Set.Icc 1 n ∧ Monotone a ∧ HasDistinctSumsWeak a}`.

status_issues.source_status: Proved. Hegyvári (1986) showed (1/3+o(1))n ≤ g(n) ≤ (2/3+o(1))n, which is exactly this statement. The file's own docstring also says "It is known that ...".
status_issues.evidence:
- erdosproblems.com/357 remarks: "If g(n) is the maximal k such that there are 1≤a_1,…,a_k≤n with all consecutive sums distinct ... then Hegyvári [He86] has proved that (1/3+o(1))n ≤ g(n) ≤ (2/3+o(1))n."
- [He86] is N. Hegyvári, On consecutive sums in sequences, Acta Math. Hungar. 48 (1986), 193–200 (Crossref DOI 10.1007/BF01949064).
- Beker, arXiv:2311.10087, introduction, confirms the lower bound: "Hegyvári ... showed ... that one can find a sequence of length (1/3+o(1))n in [n] with all consecutive sums distinct."
- On the source's forum, Adenwalla notes that the 2n/3 upper bound follows from Hegyvári's paper.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change to `@[category research solved, AMS 11]`. Optionally cite [He86] in the docstring.

reformulations.difference: The source says the sums ∑_{u≤i≤v} a_i are distinct over index pairs u ≤ v. The Lean instead requires J ↦ ∑_{x∈J} a x to be injective on all order-connected finsets J of the index type, and this includes J = ∅.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
On `Fin k` and `ℕ`, the nonempty order-connected finsets are exactly the intervals Icc u v with u ≤ v, one for each pair (u, v). The only extra set is ∅, whose sum is 0.
- In `f`, `g` and `h` every term lies in [1, n], so every nonempty interval sum is at least 1 and never equals 0.
- In the ℕ-indexed infinite variants, `StrictMono A` gives A i ≥ 1 for i ≥ 1. So comparing with ∅ only rules out A 0 = 0 (I checked this in Lean). The source's positive-integer setting excludes that case anyway, and A 0 = 0 would make the [0,v] and [1,v] sums coincide.
So the Lean condition is exactly "all consecutive sums are distinct".

review.notes:
**Lean checks** (scratch files in /workspace/review):
- All statements elaborate as intended: `1/3 : ℝ`, `√(n:ℝ)`, `Set.Icc` in ℤ for `f`/`h` and in ℕ for `g`, density predicates relative to `Set.univ`.
- Proved `f n ≤ n` (so the sSup is a genuine maximum) and `f 2 = 2`.
- `HasDistinctSums` excludes `A 0 = 0`. The infinite-set hypotheses can be satisfied (e.g. A i = 2^i), so those variants are not vacuous.
- Compact proof of the `h` finding, which compiles cleanly:
```lean
lemma injective_of_hasDistinctSums {ι α : Type*} [PartialOrder ι] [AddCommMonoid α] {a : ι → α}
    (ha : HasDistinctSums a) : Function.Injective a := by
  intro i j hij
  have h1 : ({i} : Finset ι) ∈ {J : Finset ι | (J : Set ι).OrdConnected} := by simp [Set.ordConnected_singleton]
  have h2 : ({j} : Finset ι) ∈ {J : Finset ι | (J : Set ι).OrdConnected} := by simp [Set.ordConnected_singleton]
  simpa using ha h1 h2 (by simp [hij])
theorem h_eq_f : h = f := by
  funext n; unfold h f; congr 1; ext k
  exact ⟨fun ⟨a, h1, h2, h3⟩ => ⟨a, h1, h2.strictMono_of_injective (injective_of_hasDistinctSums h3), h3⟩,
    fun ⟨a, h1, h2, h3⟩ => ⟨a, h1, h2.monotone, h3⟩⟩
```

**`erdos_357.variants.weisenberg`** is stated correctly and is true. The interval [n−m, n] has all consecutive sums distinct whenever r(m−r) < n−m for every r, which allows m ≈ 2√n − 2. I checked this by computation for n = 100..1200 (19..68 terms), so f(n) ≥ 2√n − O(1).

**Not reported:**
- `parts.i`, `infinite_set_density` and `infinite_set_sum` state the source's questions as positive assertions instead of `answer(sorry) ↔ …`. CONTRIBUTING prefers `answer(sorry)`, but the problem to decide is the same. Their docstrings say \"it is conjectured\" where the source says Erdős \"asks whether\".
- The `parts.ii.*` family (and its monotone copy) admits trivial answers. The file's own note acknowledges this, and it fits CONTRIBUTING's `answer` conventions.
- The last paragraph of the page (the least non-representable m; whether ∑ 1/a_i ≪ 1) and the Coppersmith–Phillips bound are not formalized (there is a TODO). Leaving them out is not a misformalization.

**Status:** erdosproblems.com still records the main problem as OPEN as of the 2026-08-24 snapshot. There is a link to \"1 claimed proof\", but no solution has been accepted. This matches `research open`.

**Sources I could not read:** the primary sources [Er77c], [ErGr80] and [He86]. The Rényi archive's Er77c link points to a different paper, and Springer blocks scripted clients. I checked the statements against erdosproblems.com, its forum, and Beker's arXiv paper.

**Confidence on the `h` finding:** it is 0.6 even though h = f is proved. The source's weak-monotonicity remark is loosely worded, and the forum shows even the maintainers were unsure how to read it. But the source says repeated terms are allowed, and the Lean definition makes them impossible.

demonstrated.claim: `theorem h_eq_f : Erdos357.h = Erdos357.f` is proved in a few lines, and a second example shows why: `HasDistinctSums` compares one-term intervals, so it rejects the monotone sequence (1, 1) with values in [1, 1]; the 'weakly monotone' function therefore never admits a_i = a_j and is identically the strictly monotone f.
`type_of% @Erdos357.erdos_357.variants.monotone.parts.i ↔ type_of% @Erdos357.erdos_357.parts.i` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, so this 'variant' is exactly the original question 'is f(n) = o(n)?'.

For every candidate answer G (the `answer(sorry)` slot, kept abstract to avoid `sorry`), `G =O[atTop] h` ↔ `G =O[atTop] f` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, so this is the statement of `erdos_357.parts.ii.bigO_version`.
For every candidate answer G, `h =O[atTop] G` ↔ `f =O[atTop] G` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, so this is the statement of `erdos_357.parts.ii.bigO_version_symm`.
For every candidate answer G, `h =Θ[atTop] G` ↔ `f =Θ[atTop] G` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, so this is the statement of `erdos_357.parts.ii.bigTheta_version`.
For every candidate answer G, `G =o[atTop] h` ↔ `G =o[atTop] f` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, so this is the statement of `erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version`.
For every candidate answer G, `h =o[atTop] G` ↔ `f =o[atTop] G` closes by `rw [h_eq_f]`, so this is the statement of `erdos_357.parts.ii.littleO_version_symm`.

submission.summary: `/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean` proves `Erdos357.h = Erdos357.f` in about 10 lines. `HasDistinctSums` compares the one-term intervals {i} and {j}, which forces injectivity, and `Monotone` plus injective gives `StrictMono`. It also checks that the monotone sequence (1, 1) with values in [1, 1] is rejected, even though the source's variant says 'we allow a_i = a_j'. From `h_eq_f` it follows that `variants.monotone.parts.i` is literally `parts.i` (stated with `type_of%` of both declarations). Each of the five `variants.monotone.parts.ii.*` statements equals its `parts.ii.*` counterpart for every value of the answer slot; that slot is kept as an arbitrary G, because `type_of%` would bring in the canonical `sorryAx`. The file compiles with zero messages and uses only the standard axioms. The Hegyvári category mismatch was reported only as a status issue, not a misformalization, so it is not demonstrated here.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«357»

/-! Erdős 357: the "weakly monotone" function `Erdos357.h` is identically `Erdos357.f`. -/

open Filter Asymptotics

/-- `HasDistinctSums` compares the one-term intervals `{i}`, `{j}`, so it forces distinct terms. -/
lemma injective_of_hasDistinctSums {ι α : Type*} [PartialOrder ι] [AddCommMonoid α]
    {a : ι → α} (ha : Erdos357.HasDistinctSums a) : Function.Injective a := by
  intro i j hij
  have h1 : ({i} : Finset ι) ∈ {J : Finset ι | (J : Set ι).OrdConnected} := by
    simp [Set.ordConnected_singleton]
  have h2 : ({j} : Finset ι) ∈ {J : Finset ι | (J : Set ι).OrdConnected} := by
    simp [Set.ordConnected_singleton]
  simpa using ha h1 h2 (by simp [hij])

-- Erdos357.h: the definition meant to allow repeated terms (a_i = a_j) is equal to the strictly
-- monotone `Erdos357.f` at every `n`: `Monotone` plus the forced injectivity is `StrictMono`.
theorem h_eq_f : Erdos357.h = Erdos357.f := by
  funext n; unfold Erdos357.h Erdos357.f; congr 1; ext k
  exact ⟨fun ⟨a, h1, h2, h3⟩ =>

Added `HasDistinctSumsWeak` (two different intervals must have different sums unless both have at most one term, the reading suggested on the source's forum) and used it in `h`, so repeated terms are allowed as the source says. Added a proved `@[category test, AMS 11]` theorem `hasDistinctSumsWeak_one_one` showing (1, 1) is accepted. Updated the docstring of `h` (chosen reading, why the old condition collapses to f, forum link) and, as consequential edits, the six `variants.monotone.*` docstrings. Statements, categories and AMS tags are unchanged. The existing comment about uncertain relative difficulty is now accurate, so it was kept. Checked on a copy of the edited file: every admissible length satisfies k ≤ 2n (the sSup is a genuine maximum), 2 ≤ h 1 (so h ≠ f), and the forum's example (1, 1, 2) is rejected. The file compiles with only the 17 expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. The separately reported status issue (`erdos_357.variants.hegyvari` still tagged `research open` although Hegyvári proved it in 1986) was left unchanged, since it is a status update rather than a misformalization.

def HasDistinctSums {ι α : Type*} [Preorder ι] [AddCommMonoid α] (a : ι → α) : Prop :=
  {J : Finset ι | (J : Set ι).OrdConnected}.InjOn (fun J ↦ ∑ x ∈ J, a x)

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. -/
noncomputable def f (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | ∃ a : Fin k → ℤ, Set.range a ⊆ Set.Icc 1 n ∧ StrictMono a ∧ HasDistinctSums a}

/-- Let $f(n)$ be the maximal $k$ such that there exist integers $1 \le a_1 < \dotsc < a_k \le n$
such that all sums of the shape $\sum_{u \le i \le v} a_i$ are distinct. Is $f(n)=o(n)$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_357.parts.i : (fun n ↦ (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n ↦ (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

together with a proof of the theorem, but providing a *mathematically interesting* answer.
Note also that there might be other reasonable (and non equivalent) formal statements that capture this
question.
Similar remarks hold for the `variants.monotone` formalisations later in this file.

/-- A weakening of `HasDistinctSums` that allows repeated terms: sums over two different
order-connected sets must differ unless both sets have at most one element. -/
def HasDistinctSumsWeak {ι α : Type*} [Preorder ι] [AddCommMonoid α] (a : ι → α) : Prop :=
  ∀ J₁ J₂ : Finset ι, (J₁ : Set ι).OrdConnected → (J₂ : Set ι).OrdConnected → J₁ ≠ J₂ →
    (2 ≤ J₁.card ∨ 2 ≤ J₂.card) → ∑ x ∈ J₁, a x ≠ ∑ x ∈ J₂, a x

/-- Unlike `HasDistinctSums`, the weak condition admits repeated terms, e.g. $(1, 1)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem hasDistinctSumsWeak_one_one : HasDistinctSumsWeak ![(1 : ℤ), 1] := by
  intro J₁ J₂ _ _ hne hcard
  have key : ∀ J : Finset (Fin 2), J = ∅ ∨ J = {0} ∨ J = {1} ∨ J = Finset.univ := by decide
  rcases key J₁ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases key J₂ with rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl <;>
    simp_all [Fin.sum_univ_two]

sums may coincide (so $a_i = a_j$ is allowed).

give back $f$. Following the discussion of this variant at
https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/357, two one-term sums are not compared. -/
noncomputable def h (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {k : ℕ | ∃ a : Fin k → ℤ, Set.range a ⊆ Set.Icc 1 n ∧ Monotone a ∧ HasDistinctSumsWeak a}
